name: Glyptothek
overview: Museum of Greek and Roman marble sculpture on the north side of Königsplatz in Munich's Kunstareal, facing the State Collections of Antiquities; the museum calls itself Munich's oldest public museum and the only museum in the world dedicated exclusively to ancient sculpture (museum website; German Wikipedia).

Built from 1816 to 1830 by Leo von Klenze, court architect to Ludwig I, King of Bavaria from 1825 to 1848, whom the museum names as its founder and benefactor; fourteen halls surround a square courtyard (museum website).
Closed at the outbreak of the Second World War, hit by bombing in 1944, rebuilt from the 1960s to the plain brick look Johann Martin von Wagner had proposed, and reopened in 1972 (museum website).
funding_verdict: Glyptothek: public: a state museum of the Free State of Bavaria, with a friends' association

name: Lothringer 13 Halle
overview: Exhibition space for international and local contemporary art at Lothringer Strasse 13 in Haidhausen, near Weissenburger Platz, with about 700 square metres for changing group shows (muenchen.de; City of Munich).

Founded in 1980 as the "Künstlerwerkstatt" in a former machine factory; more than 200 exhibitions by over 1,000 artists followed, among them Louise Lawler, Fischli/Weiss, Albert Oehlen and Gregor Schneider (German Wikipedia).
The exhibition rooms are in a former engine-grinding workshop (Motorenschleiferei) in a rear building; the front building holds a research and information room also used for events (City of Munich).
funding_verdict: Lothringer 13 Halle: public: a cultural institution of the Kulturreferat of the City of Munich

name: Museum Brandhorst
overview: Museum Brandhorst is a museum of contemporary art in the Kunstareal in Munich, in a building by the Berlin architects Sauerbruch Hutton whose facade is made of 36,000 ceramic rods in 23 colours (museum website).

It shows the collection of Udo and Anette Brandhorst, which was transferred to a foundation in 1993; a cooperation agreement between the foundation and the Free State of Bavaria followed in 1999 and the museum opened in 2009 as part of the Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen (museum website).

What is there: over 2,000 works of 20th and 21st century art, with a focus on US art since the 1960s; holdings of Cy Twombly including the 'Lepanto' cycle (2001) and 'Untitled (Roses)' (2008); over 120 works by Andy Warhol, among them 'Round Marilyn' (1962), 'Mustard Race Riot' (1963) and 'The Last Supper' (1986); groups of works by Keith Haring, Mike Kelley, Louise Lawler, Cady Noland and Kara Walker; and the Eva Felten Fotosammlung, about 450 works given in 2021 (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museum Brandhorst: state-run building and operations, private foundation for acquisitions
wider_context: The museum is part of the Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen. The Süddeutsche Zeitung reported on 19/20 February 2025 on a list of about 200 works in the Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen suspected of being Nazi-looted art, and that descendants of dispossessed Jewish owners had not been told (Jüdische Allgemeine, 2 April 2025; Staatsgemäldesammlungen statement, 26 February 2025).

On 2 April 2025 Bavaria's arts minister Markus Blume (CSU) announced that director general Bernhard Maaz would leave his post and work at the Zentralinstitut für Kunstgeschichte, with Anton Biebl, former head of culture for the City of Munich, as interim head; Blume called the internal state of the collections 'unzufriedenstellend' and said a public prosecutor had been assigned to clear up the allegations (Jüdische Allgemeine, 2 April 2025; epd in Sonntagsblatt, 2 April 2025).

name: Neues Museum Nürnberg
aliases: Neues Museum, Staatliches Museum für Kunst und Design in Nürnberg
overview: The Neues Museum is a state museum for art and design at Klarissenplatz, Nuremberg (museum website).
It opened in April 2000 and is run by the Free State of Bavaria and the city of Nuremberg; the architect was Volker Staab of Berlin (museum website; Museen in Bayern).

What is there: more than 3,000 square metres of collection and exhibition space (Museen in Bayern). Current programme: Double Up! (art and design), a Günther Förg show and a Gerhard Richter show, and Mein Balkan, a donation by René Block (museum website). The pages read gave no object count.
funding_verdict: Neues Museum Nürnberg: public, Free State of Bavaria and the city of Nuremberg; no amounts on the pages read.

name: Kunsthalle Würth
overview: Kunsthalle Würth is one of the art venues of the Würth Group, which makes fastening and assembly technology and has its headquarters in Künzelsau-Gaisbach (Schwäbische Zeitung, 17 June 2026).

Reinhold Würth built the collection; the German houses are Hirschwertscheuer in Künzelsau (1989), Museum Würth in Künzelsau-Gaisbach (1991), Kunsthalle Würth in Schwäbisch Hall (2001), the Johanniterkirche in Schwäbisch Hall (2008) and Museum Würth 2 in Künzelsau (2020, by David Chipperfield, with a concert hall) (Schwäbische Zeitung, 17 June 2026).

What is there: the Sammlung Würth spans about 500 years from the late Middle Ages to the 21st century with more than 20,000 works, shaped by Würth's personal interests (Schwäbische Zeitung, 17 June 2026); the Stuttgarter Zeitung quotes the collection's growth from 500 to 21,000 works (Stuttgarter Zeitung, interview with Maria Würth).
funding_verdict: Würth museums: corporate, paid by the Würth Group; no budget stated

name: Künstlerhaus Stuttgart
overview: Contemporary art centre at Reuchlinstraße 4b in Stuttgart (address on the Künstlerhaus site), in the west of the city, in a former suitcase factory with four floors and about 600 m² of exhibition space (German Wikipedia).

Founded by Stuttgart artists in 1978 (stated by the Künstlerhaus; German Wikipedia). Art historian Hans Dieter Huber has written scholarly texts on the institution and its building (stated by the Künstlerhaus).

Organised as a registered association, Künstlerhaus Reuchlinstraße e.V. (Stuttgart council paper GRDrs 170/2024). The board is Ania Corcilius (first chairperson), Jochen Detscher (deputy) and Christoph Schwerdtfeger (treasurer). Juliane Gebhardt is managing director. Tamarind Rossetti and Stephen Wright have been artistic directors since 1 January 2024 (stated by the Künstlerhaus).
funding_verdict: Künstlerhaus Stuttgart: public: City of Stuttgart institutional grant, plus project support from foundations and partners

name: Hong Kong Heritage Museum
overview: The Hong Kong Heritage Museum is at 1 Man Lam Road, Sha Tin, and its website footer credits the Leisure and Cultural Services Department (museum FAQ page).
The pages read did not state who founded it or when it opened.
What is there: the pages read do not give a collection count; they say visitors can access data on the museum's collection with computers in the Resource Centre (museum FAQ page).
funding_verdict: Hong Kong Heritage Museum: public: a government department, free permanent exhibitions

name: Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri)
overview: Municipal art museum at Kaupvangsstræti 8 on Listagil, Akureyri's Art Street, which also holds artist-run spaces, residencies, an art school and design studios (museum website; 2019 programme).
Founded in 1993; 2026 is its 33rd exhibition year (2019 and 2026 programmes).
The building first housed the KEA co-operative dairy, Mjólkursamlag KEA (Hönnunarmiðstöð, 2018).
funding_verdict: Akureyri Art Museum: public: the town of Akureyri, with state money under a cultural agreement

name: Nýló (The Living Art Museum / Nýlistasafnið)
overview: Artist-run museum and exhibition space for contemporary art in Marshall House (Marshallhúsið), Grandagarður 20, Reykjavík. The Strætó 14 bus stops at Grandi (museum website).

Founded in 1978 by a group of artists, mainly linked to Fluxus and conceptual art, with a gallery added in 1981 (Wikipedia). Reykjavík City's 2016 notice says 27 artists founded it. Wikipedia says 26.

The collection holds over 2,200 works from the 1960s to the present, donated by artists, collectors and people connected to the museum (museum website). Giulia Nestola writes that the museum is not allowed to buy artworks (museum website, 22 July 2026).
funding_verdict: Nýló: supported by the Icelandic state, the City of Reykjavík, and private and voluntary donations

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
aliases: Prince of Wales Museum of Western India
overview: An art and history museum on the Crescent Site at the southern tip of Mumbai, formerly the Prince of Wales Museum of Western India, in an Indo-Saracenic building by the Scottish architect George Wittet, a Grade I heritage building within the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensemble that UNESCO listed in 2018 (museum website).

Citizens of Bombay resolved on 14 August 1905 to build it as a memorial to the Prince of Wales's visit, and he laid the foundation stone on 11 November 1905. A Board of Trustees was constituted by Act III of 1909, the building was completed in 1914 and handed to the Trustees in 1920, the museum opened on 10 January 1922, an extension wing opened in 1938, and it took its present name in 2001 (museum website, History).

What is there: about 70,000 objects from the Stone Age to the present, among them sculptures, terracottas, bronzes, finds from Indus Valley excavations and miniature paintings (museum website). The pages read did not give the sections or the origin of individual collections.
funding_verdict: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya: private and corporate donors, foundations and one central government grant; by its own account it takes no state operating aid

name: Tower of David Museum
overview: Museum of the history of Jerusalem in the citadel by Jaffa Gate in the Old City (Associated Press; Wikipedia).
Opened in 1989 by the Jerusalem Foundation (Wikipedia).
The citadel was rebuilt by the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad in 1310 and expanded by Suleiman the Magnificent between 1537 and 1541 (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Tower of David Museum: philanthropy led by the Clore Israel Foundation, with the city and two ministries as partners in the renewal
wider_context: Status of the site: Israel captured East Jerusalem, including the Old City, from Jordan in the 1967 war and annexed it, a step that is not internationally recognised; Palestinians seek East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state (Associated Press). The museum stands inside the Old City.

Rockefeller Museum: a December 2023 document, confirmed by a Heritage Ministry spokesperson, lists selling or leasing the Rockefeller Museum to private entities for a hotel as an option. David Gurevich of Ariel University, a member of Israel's Archaeology Council, said there is an attempt to turn it into a luxury hotel (Times of Israel, 13 December 2025).

Lieber said her museum's interest in the Rockefeller is historical and cultural, and the museum says it takes no part in the discussions about that building's future (Times of Israel). The dispute concerns the Rockefeller, where the Tower of David Museum only runs tours.

press_items.title: Ilan Ben Zion, "Jerusalem's redesigned Tower of David Museum opens after 3-year renovation" (2023)
Somdeep Sen, "How Israel weaponises museums to erase Palestinian existence" (2023)

name: Habima Theatre
overview: Israel's national theatre, on Habima Square in central Tel Aviv (Wikipedia).

Founded as an amateur Hebrew troupe by Nahum Zemach in Białystok in 1912; it left the Soviet Union in 1926 and settled in Palestine in 1931 (Wikipedia). Its tradition began in Moscow in 1918 (N12); there Stanislavsky made it a studio of the Moscow Art Theatre, and it premiered "The Dybbuk" on 31 January 1922 (Hebrew Wikipedia).
It built its Tel Aviv house in 1945 and has been the official national theatre since 1958, when it received the Israel Prize (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Habima Theatre: public: Tel Aviv-Yafo municipality and Israel's Culture Ministry
wider_context: On 10 November 2016 Habima staged Agnon's "A Simple Story" in the settlement of Kiryat Arba near Hebron, against opposition from supporters of the theatre and left-wing groups; one actor refused to perform for ideological reasons (JTA).
Before the show Breaking the Silence took some actors on a tour of Hebron; Regev posted "Well done, Habima. Well done, Kiryat Arba" and promised shows in Bet El, Elkana and Ariel (JTA).

In September 2010, as more than 30 artists declared a boycott of the new Ariel cultural centre, Habima co-manager Odelia Friedman told a Knesset committee that "residents of Ariel are residents of Israel and Habima will stage shows for them" (Arutz Sheva, a partisan outlet, 2 September 2010).

On 29 March 2012 actors and directors including Emma Thompson, Mike Leigh and Jonathan Miller asked Shakespeare's Globe in a Guardian letter to withdraw Habima's invitation to its Globe to Globe festival, citing its "shameful record of involvement with illegal Israeli settlements" (letter reprinted by Mondoweiss, an advocacy outlet).
These disputes concern Habima's own performances under the funding rules of its state funder.

name: Fondazione Antonio Ratti
overview: Non-profit foundation for textiles and contemporary art, based at Villa Sucota, via per Cernobbio 19, Como, on Lake Como (the foundation's website).

Created in 1985 by the silk industrialist Antonio Ratti to share his passion for art and textiles and to preserve his textile collection. His daughter Annie Ratti has headed it since 2002 (the foundation's website).

Named for Antonio Ratti, born in Como in 1915, who founded the silk firm Tessitura Serica Antonio Ratti in 1945 and in 1995 funded the Antonio Ratti Textile Center at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York (the foundation's website).
funding_verdict: Fondazione Antonio Ratti: private: created by textile industrialist Antonio Ratti, headed by his daughter, with sponsors for projects

name: Centrale Fies
overview: Research centre for contemporary performance practices at Loc. Fies 1, Dro, in the Trentino province (Luoghi del contemporaneo, Italian Ministry of Culture).

Run by the cooperative Il Gaviale società cooperativa, via Gramsci 13, Dro, named as operator in the footer of the centre's website. The project was launched in 1999 by Barbara Boninsegna and Dino Sommadossi together with Il Gaviale, building on the Drodesera festival, which began in 1980 (Centrale Fies).

Housed in an early twentieth-century hydroelectric plant, partly still active, owned by Hydro Dolomiti Energia (Lampoon Magazine, Eugenia Pacelli, 18 September 2024). The centre says it was among the first in Italy to repurpose industrial archaeology for artistic and cultural use.
funding_verdict: Centrale Fies: public and private by the centre's own account: Autonomous Province of Trento, Autonomous Region of Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol, Ministry of Culture, Municipality of Dro, EU Culture Programme, Hydro Dolomiti Energia, Cassa Rurale Alto Garda and Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Trento e Rovereto

name: Museo Nazionale del Bargello
overview: The Museo Nazionale del Bargello is a museum in Florence's oldest public palace, run with four other sites by the GAMB institute (Galleria dell'Accademia di Firenze e Musei del Bargello) (museum website).
The Bargello and the Galleria dell'Accademia merged following a 2024 ministerial decree and took the name GAMB in May 2026 (Il Sole 24 Ore, 6 October 2026).

What is there: the site describes the institute as 7 museums with a collection of 50,632 artistic objects, among them sculpture, paintings, tapestries, ivories, jewellery, maiolica, coins, musical instruments and antique weapons; the sites are the Bargello, Cappelle Medicee (the Medici burial place with Michelangelo's Sagrestia Nuova), Orsanmichele (a sculpture museum above a former market and church), Palazzo Davanzati (a 14th century house restored by Elia Volpi) and Casa Martelli (closed for works until 31 December 2026) (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Nazionale del Bargello: state museum with Art Bonus and foundation support for restorations.

name: Pinacoteca Ambrosiana
overview: The Veneranda Biblioteca Ambrosiana in Milan combines a Pinacoteca, a Biblioteca, an Accademia and a Crypt, and also looks after the Roman Forum and the Church of San Sepolcro (museum website).
It dates from 1609 and is tied to Cardinal Federico Borromeo; the library opened to the public in 1609 (museum website; Artribune, 31 January 2026).

What is there: the highlights named are Leonardo da Vinci's Portrait of a Musician, Caravaggio's Basket of Fruit, Raphael's cartoon for The School of Athens, Botticelli's Madonna of the Pavilion, Titian's Adoration of the Magi and the Codex Atlanticus; Artribune adds a Virgil manuscript with a miniature by Simone Martini (museum website; Artribune, 31 January 2026).
funding_verdict: Pinacoteca Ambrosiana: private-public mix of ticket income, corporate and foundation sponsors, with no state grant named.

name: Gallerie Estensi
overview: The Gallerie Estensi are a 'museo diffuso' with four sites: the Galleria Estense and the Biblioteca Estense Universitaria in Modena, the Museo Lapidario Estense in Modena and the Palazzo Ducale in Sassuolo (museum website).

The Pinacoteca Nazionale di Ferrara belongs to the Musei Nazionali di Ferrara from 1 January 2026 (museum website). The ministry created the autonomous institute in 2015 and Martina Bagnoli directed it from then until 2023 (Finestre sull'Arte).
What is there: the online collection covers the Galleria Estense, the Palazzo Ducale, the Pinacoteca Nazionale and the Museo Lapidario Estense (museum website). The pages read gave no count of works.
funding_verdict: Gallerie Estensi: state institute with its own ticket income and private contributions.

name: Fondazione Morra Greco
overview: Contemporary art centre for exhibitions, research and international artist residencies in the historic centre of Naples, in Palazzo Caracciolo di Avellino (the foundation's website).

Established in 2003 by the dentist and collector Maurizio Morra Greco and opened to the public in 2006 with an exhibition by Gregor Schneider. It grew out of the Collezione Morra Greco, begun in the 1990s, which holds over a thousand works by about two hundred artists (the foundation's history page).

Building: a sixteenth-century residence that was once a Benedictine convent, with a five-bay cloister. The poet Torquato Tasso lived there from 1550 to 1554, and Giacomo del Po painted illusory architectural frescoes on the first floor in the early eighteenth century. The palazzo was sold in 1806 and divided. Morra Greco began acquiring units in 1996, and ancient Greek walls were found in the basement (the foundation's venue page).
funding_verdict: Fondazione Morra Greco: public-private: founder Maurizio Morra Greco and the Region of Campania

name: Teatro Regio di Parma
overview: Opera house at Strada Garibaldi 16/a, Parma (theatre website).
What is there: opera seasons and the Festival Verdi, with Festival Verdi 2027, Verdi Off 2027 and Verdi Off Los Angeles announced (theatre website).
Archive: the site lists a performance archive, a training archive and a festival archive (theatre website).
funding_verdict: Teatro Regio di Parma: public partners plus named corporate sponsors; amounts not stated on the pages read

name: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Reggio Calabria (MArRC)
aliases: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Reggio Calabria
overview: State archaeological museum in Palazzo Piacentini, Piazza De Nava 26, in the centre of Reggio Calabria, next to Reggio Lido station and facing the Strait of Messina (museum website; Ministry of Culture).
Marcello Piacentini designed the building in the 1930s as one of the first in Europe made for an archaeological collection; the museum opened in part in 1954 and officially in 1959 (museum website).
An underwater archaeology section was created in 1981 for the Riace Bronzes, two 5th-century BC Greek warriors found off Riace Marina in August 1972, restored in Reggio and Florence (museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Reggio Calabria: public: the Italian Ministry of Culture, with EU recovery funds
wider_context: Renovation overrun, 2009 to 2016: the Bronzes were due back on display in March 2011 but returned only at the end of December 2013, and the renovation's cost rose from 11 million to 30 million euros (The Art Newspaper, February 2014).

In 2012 the historian Franco Cardini proposed moving the Bronzes to Florence, backed by Mayor Renzi and Culture Undersecretary Roberto Cecchi; the Calabria Region called the idea unworkable (Panorama).
The museum ran the overrun renovation and holds the Bronzes these proposals concerned.

press_items.title: "The Riace bronze warriors back on their feet at last" (2014)
"Valorizzazione Bronzi di Riace, è polemica tra Sgarbi e il Comitato per i Bronzi" (2022)
